technique.how: Count chest-wall excursions for a full 60 seconds while the patient is at rest and unaware (e.g., while appearing to take the pulse). Do not use the triage estimate or a 15-second count multiplied; record the pattern (deep Kussmaul vs shallow rapid) as well as the rate.
technique.prerequisites: Patient at rest for several minutes; not talking.

interpretation.positive_finding: RR above threshold raises the probability of radiographic pneumonia (pooled LR+ 3.5 for RR >=20-24) and is a qSOFA/CURB-65 criterion; deep regular tachypnea points to metabolic acidosis or uremia.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal rate lowers but does not exclude pneumonia (LR- 0.77); absence of any vital-sign abnormality lowers CAP probability more strongly (LR- 0.25).
interpretation.pitfalls: Recorded rates are often estimated rather than counted, clustering at 18-20. Pain, anxiety, fever and hypoxia raise the rate nonspecifically; PE frequently presents with RR >20 but the finding is not discriminating.
interpretation.changes_what: RR >24 with fever/cough: image for pneumonia and assess severity. Normal vitals in low-risk cough: CXR may be deferred. Unexplained tachypnea: check gas/lactate for acidosis.

estimates.target_condition: Radiographic community-acquired pneumonia (respiratory rate >=20/min; >=22 in one study, >=24 in two)
estimates.population: Adults with respiratory symptoms in primary care, no serious illness; 6 studies, n=4,468
estimates.location: Table 2 (PMC6527561 full text); footnote ¥ gives thresholds

estimates.target_condition: Community-acquired pneumonia (absence of ANY abnormal vital sign, composite including respiratory rate)
estimates.population: Adults with suspected pneumonia or acute cough; 17 prospective cohorts (9 primary care, 7 ED)
estimates.quote: it is decreased most by the absence of abnormal vital signs (LR- = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.11 to 0.48)

sources.citation: Htun TP, Sun Y, Chua HL, Pang J. Clinical features for diagnosis of pneumonia among adults in primary care setting: A systematic and meta-review. Sci Rep. 2019;9:7600.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a normal RR to exclude PE, sepsis or acidosis; do not rely on charted (estimated) rates.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: RR >=30, or RR >=22 with altered mentation or SBP <=100 (qSOFA >=2), or tachypnea with rising PCO2/fatigue: escalate to higher level of care.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Charted RR is frequently estimated rather than counted; a 60-s count is required for reproducibility (vital-sign reliability discussed in Metlay 1997).

extraction_notes: Primary numeric estimate is the pooled RR row from Htun 2019 Table 2 (PMC OA); the pooled threshold is >=20 with two studies at >=24 and one at >=22, so it does not exactly match the record's >24 title. Ebell 2020 composite 'absence of abnormal vital signs' LR- quoted from abstract as the rule-out anchor; RR-specific rows from Ebell tables not visible. Metlay 1997 RCE and Chunilal 2003 PE RCE cited as context; neither abstract contains an RR-specific number.
